# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

# [cookie] recent context, ⟦CMEM_NOW_HEADER:69b195c00d2e⟧

Stats: 2 obs (985t read) | 11,344t work | 91% savings

### Nov 3, 2026
9 2:03p ○ Existing maxAge validation and docs locations in cookie library
10 2:04p ◆ stringifySetCookie rejects maxAge above 400 days
S3 Reject `stringifySetCookie` calls with `maxAge` over 400 days (34,560,000 seconds) by throwing a TypeError, with matching tests and README documentation. (Nov 3, 2:04 PM)
**Investigated**: The cookie library's `maxAge` handling in `src/index.ts`, including the integer check in `stringifySetCookie`, the `maxAgeRegExp` parser used for Set-Cookie headers, and the option JSDoc. Also the README `maxAge` section and the existing `maxAge` tests in `src/stringify-set-cookie.spec.ts` and `src/parse-set-cookie.spec.ts`.

**Learned**: Before the change, `stringifySetCookie` only checked that `maxAge` was an integer, so values above 400 days were serialized unchanged and browsers silently shortened them. The existing error message prefix is "option maxAge is invalid", and the new check reuses it.

**Completed**: In `src/index.ts`, a `MAX_MAX_AGE` constant (400 × 24 × 60 × 60) was added. `stringifySetCookie` now throws a TypeError when `maxAge` exceeds it, and the `maxAge` JSDoc notes the limit. In `src/stringify-set-cookie.spec.ts`, two tests were added: 34,560,001 throws, and 34,560,000 serializes as `Max-Age=34560000`. In `README.md`, a note under `maxAge` documents the limit. The diff is 3 files, 27 insertions. The vitest run reported 63,742 tests passing across 4 files. The `tsc --noEmit` output was empty in the captured tail, which is consistent with a clean compile. Nothing has been committed.

**Next Steps**: The session is ongoing and no further work has been started. Likely next steps are reviewing the diff and deciding whether to commit. The work so far covers only the stringify side, and `parseSetCookie` still accepts any `Max-Age` value.

**Notes**: The limit is enforced only in `stringifySetCookie`, so a parsed Set-Cookie header with a larger `Max-Age` is still accepted. This is a deliberate scope choice that follows the user's request, which named only `stringifySetCookie`.
